sections.h2: What makes a Midland house sale different from other Michigan sales?
sections.html:
Midland runs its own rental certification program, publishes its own tax calendar and sits in a county with a flat deed recording fee. A seller who knows those three items can price and schedule a sale without surprises.

The city's 2025 estimate is 42,806 people, a gain of 0.3% over the 2020 base, spread over 34.37 square miles of land at about 1,238 per square mile. Homeowners occupy 67.1% of the 18,535 households counted for 2020 to 2024. The median owner-occupied value is $203,900, and median gross rent is $1,048.

Household income has a median of $73,325, and 44.6% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The poverty rate is 10.3% and the average commute takes 20 minutes. About 20.4% of residents are 65 or older, and 21.2% are under 18.

sections.h2: Where is Midland and what drives its housing?
sections.html:
Midland is the Midland County seat, built where the Chippewa River joins the Tittabawassee. It lies roughly 24 miles northwest of Saginaw and 19 miles west of Bay City, and a small piece of the city reaches into Bay County.

Dow Chemical, founded in the city in 1897, is the anchor employer, and its 2,600-acre Michigan Operations Industrial Park along Bay City Road supports about 6,000 employees and contractors. Tenants there include Corteva Agriscience, Hemlock Semiconductor and DuPont. Health care and education follow, with a 324-bed hospital in the MyMichigan system and Northwood University, while Midland Public Schools and Bullock Creek Public Schools cover K-12.

The city counts more than 35 neighborhoods, grouped by the city into eight general areas:

  • Downtown, including the Circle business district dating from 1938
  • North Side and Midland West, near the parks and river corridors
  • Country Club, known for large wooded lots
  • East End, where a Midtown revival started in 2018
  • Industrial Park and the small South area around the old Mapleton depot
  • West Main Street Historic District, set up in 1979

In the historic district, a commission reviews construction, additions, alterations, repairs, moves and demolitions, so check with it before planning visible work. Drivers use US-10 along the north edge, M-20 toward Mount Pleasant and M-47 toward Saginaw and MBS International Airport. Midland has no regular scheduled bus; Dial-A-Ride operates within city limits.

sections.h2: Does the May 2020 flood matter to a Midland buyer?
sections.html:
It often does, because lenders and buyers ask about it. On May 19, 2020, the Edenville and Sanford dams failed, and about 10,000 Midland residents were evacuated during what was described as a 500-year flood.

If your house took water or stands near either river, assemble repair invoices, permits, insurance claims and remediation records before you list or request an offer. Paper that explains a repaired basement is easier to price than a basement nobody can account for.

Ordinary weather also leaves marks. Midland averages 33.41 inches of precipitation and 31.4 inches of snow a year, with January highs near 29 degrees, so roofs, gutters and furnaces get a real test each winter.

sections.h2: What does Midland require of a house that has been a rental?
sections.html:
Midland inspects and certifies each home, duplex, rooming house, short-term rental and apartment that its owner does not occupy, and the unit may not be rented until certified. That includes houses where no rent is collected and houses occupied by relatives.

An owner living in a single-family house can take up to two boarders without an inspection, but more than two renters triggers one. No more than four unrelated tenants may share a rental unit. The schedule that took effect July 1, 2025 is:

  • Rooming house: $105
  • Other rental units: $79 for the first unit and $36 for each extra unit
  • First reinspection per unit: free, with later ones billed at the certification rate
  • Late certification: $36 per unit, and the full certification fee again after 30 and after 60 days of delay

Questions go to the Rental Program at (989) 837-3383, option 1, or rentalprogram@midland-mi.org. If you plan to rent the house for a few months before a sale, the certificate has to come first.

sections.h2: Which Midland tax dates should a seller watch?
sections.html:
Midland mails summer bills on July 1 and winter bills on December 1, and December 31 is Tax Day, the date that fixes the next year's value and classification. The city posts the full calendar and notes that the dates stay close to constant.

Midland tax calendar
DateWhat happens
February 14Prior year's winter taxes due without penalty
March 1Unpaid real property taxes pass to the Midland County Treasurer
2nd Monday in MarchBoard of Review hears value and classification appeals
June 1Principal residence exemption filing deadline for the summer bill
September 15Summer taxes due; deadline to file a summer deferment
November 1Principal residence exemption filing deadline for the winter bill

Source: City of Midland, Important Tax Related Dates. A buyer who owns and lives in the house by June 1 can claim the exemption on the summer bill, and one who does so by November 1 can claim it on the winter bill. Taxable value resets after a sale under MCL 211.27a, so expect the buyer's first bill to differ from yours.

sections.h2: What happens at the Midland County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 for any document, however many pages it has. The office sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street and keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • Warranty deeds and land contracts need a $5 tax certificate proving taxes are current.
  • State and county transfer tax is charged on the sale amount, at $4.30 per $500 combined.
  • Copies cost $1 a page, and a certified copy adds $5 to that.
  • Qualified submitters can e-record, though court orders and death certificates need a raised seal and must be filed on paper.
  • Staff do not prepare deeds or give legal advice, so work through a title company or attorney.

A deed from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild is exempt from the state transfer tax under MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: Which sale route suits a Midland house?
sections.html:
Match the route to your timeline and the house's condition. A listing suits a house in good shape with time to spare, a private sale suits an owner willing to handle the work, and a cash purchase suits a house with tenants, flood repairs or an unfinished rental certification.

Tell us the Midland address and what the house needs, and we will quote a price for it as it stands. Weigh that figure against what a listing would net after repairs and fees.

faqs.q: May I rent my Midland house out while it is for sale?
faqs.a: Yes, but only after the city inspects and certifies it. Certification costs $79 for the first unit, and late certification adds $36 per unit.

faqs.q: By what date does a Midland buyer need to claim the principal residence exemption?
faqs.a: June 1 for the summer bill and November 1 for the winter bill, provided the buyer owns and occupies the house by that date. The affidavit is filed with the city.

faqs.q: Who collects Midland taxes that go unpaid?
faqs.a: The Midland County Treasurer. Real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 are turned over to the county.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Midland deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document, plus $5 for a tax certificate when the deed carries a warranty. Transfer tax is billed on top, based on the sale price.

faqs.q: Should I mention the 2020 dam failures when I sell a Midland house?
faqs.a: Yes, if your house took water or sits near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee. Buyers and lenders ask about that event, so keep repair and insurance records ready.
